bib.title: Self-Play Preference Optimization for Language Model Alignment

question: Can language-model alignment against a general (possibly intransitive) preference model be done by approximating the Nash equilibrium of a two-player constant-sum game with a simple, scalable self-play loss?
hypothesis: A square-loss regression of the policy log-ratio onto the (centred) win probability against the current policy, iterated, approximates the exponential-weights Nash update and beats pairwise-loss iterative DPO/IPO without external GPT-4 supervision.
contributions: SPPO algorithm derived from the exponential weight update, provably converging to an approximate Nash equilibrium (duality gap O(1/sqrt(T)))
A non-pairwise square-loss objective (4.6) linked to policy gradient and token-level optimal value function
Empirical gains on Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 and Llama-3-8B-Instruct with only 60k UltraFeedback prompts and a 0.4B PairRM preference model, no GPT-4 responses or preferences

method.summary: Each round, sample K=5 responses per prompt from the current policy, score all pairs with PairRM to estimate each response's win probability against the policy's own samples, and fit log(pi/pi_t) to eta*(P_hat - 1/2) with a square loss. Three rounds, each on a different third (about 20k prompts) of UltraFeedback prompts, starting from Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 or Llama-3-8B-Instruct.
method.task: preference optimisation / LLM alignment with a general preference model

datasets.name: UltraFeedback (prompts only)
datasets.split: split into three portions, one portion per iteration (about 20k prompts each); same split as Snorkel-Mistral-PairRM-DPO
datasets.preprocessing: Mistral-7B standard chat template for generation; no responses or preferences from the dataset used

datasets.name: AlpacaEval 2.0
datasets.source: Li et al. 2023b; AlpacaFarm prompts; reference GPT-4-Turbo, annotator GPT-4-Turbo

datasets.name: Open LLM Leaderboard (Arc, HellaSwag, Winogrande, MMLU, TruthfulQA, GSM8k)

other.output: relative reward s(y,y';x); P(y>y'|x)=exp(s)/(1+exp(s)); not guaranteed transitive

models.name: Mistral-7B-SPPO / Llama-3-8B-SPPO (Iter1-3)
models.init_from: previous iteration checkpoint (first epoch of each iteration)

models.name: Snorkel-Mistral-PairRM-DPO
models.init_from: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, three rounds of iterative DPO; public checkpoint

other.note: AlpacaEval 2.0 numbers taken from Yuan et al. 2024

training.objective: Square loss (4.7): E[(log(pi_theta(y|x)/pi_t(y|x)) - eta*(P_hat(y > pi_t|x) - 1/2))^2]; log-partition approximated by constant eta/2
training.epochs: number of total training epochs=18 (as printed); the model from the first epoch on the 20k prompts of each iteration is carried to the next

other.checkpoint_selection: hyperparameters selected by average win rate judged by PairRM-0.4B on a hold-out subset of UltraFeedback
other.dpo_ipo_baselines: own iterative DPO/IPO with same settings and model selection scheme; hyperparameters maximise average PairRM win rate each iteration (values not given)

inference.decoding: sampling from the current policy during data generation
inference.samples: K = 5 responses per prompt per iteration (different random seeds); win rate over all 5 samples; winner/loser pair for DPO/IPO baselines = highest/lowest PairRM score; best-of-16 re-ranking by PairRM at test time
inference.prompting: standard Mistral-7B chat template for generation

parameters.log_partition_constant: eta/2 (Appendix A: between eta/2 for fully disordered preference and about eta for fully ordered)

metrics.name: AlpacaEval 2.0 win rate (raw)
metrics.definition: win rate over GPT-4-Turbo reference responses, judged by GPT-4-Turbo, on 805 prompts

metrics.name: Avg. Len
metrics.definition: average output length of the model on AlpacaEval 2.0 (column Avg. Len; Fig 4 table labels it chars)

metrics.name: MT-Bench
metrics.definition: GPT-4 direct score of answers, 1st turn / 2nd turn / average

metrics.name: Arena-Hard-Auto-v0.1
metrics.definition: same evaluation method as AlpacaEval 2.0 on 500 queries

metrics.name: Open LLM Leaderboard average
metrics.definition: mean over Arc, TruthfulQA, WinoGrande, GSM8k, HellaSwag, MMLU

metrics.name: Pairwise win rate by PairRM
metrics.definition: PairRM-judged pairwise win rates among models (Fig 3)

eval.protocol: Single run per model as reported; no seeds, variance or significance tests stated. GPT-4 based judges for AlpacaEval 2.0/MT-Bench/Arena-Hard.

limits: Authors: approximating the optimal policy update via regression assumes an expressive model class and data that cover the input space.
Authors: approximating the log-partition factor with a constant helps only when it is close to the soft value function; eta/2 chosen, coefficient could be tuned.
Authors: experiments use one dataset (UltraFeedback) and a few benchmarks due to limited compute.
Authors concede Open LLM Leaderboard scores for Mistral decline after Iter2 for DPO, IPO and SPPO (alignment tax).
Authors do not know why MT-Bench drops in the first two Mistral iterations.
Preference oracle is a single small model (PairRM) that may favour longer outputs; evaluation judged mostly by GPT-4-family judges; no human evaluation.
Single runs, no seeds, variance or significance tests; optimizer, precision, max tokens and hold-out size not stated; epochs=18 conflicts with carrying the first-epoch checkpoint.
Theorem 4.1 assumes realizability and applies to the mixture policy; the experiments use the last iterate and only 3 rounds.

code.snippet: l_SPPO(yw,yl,x) = (a - 1/2)^2 + (b + 1/2)^2, with a = beta*log(pi_theta(yw|x)/pi_ref(yw|x)), b likewise for yl, beta = 1/eta
